newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope to return to Vatican on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Pope to return to Vatican on Tuesday.

text.p: Pope John Paul will leave hospital on Tuesday, a week after surgery to remove his appendix, the Vatican said on Monday.
"He will return to the Vatican where he will spend a period of convalescence and rest according to his doctors' orders," the Vatican said in a statement.
It added that the Pope, 76, would gradually resume his daily activities.
The statement said doctors at Rome's Gemelli hospital would remove his stitches on Tuesday morning and that the Pope would leave hospital the same day.

The Pope made his first public appearance since surgery on Sunday. He spoke for five minutes from the window of his hospital room, thanking doctors and nurses for their care and joking that the hospital had become the "third Vatican" after Saint Peter's Basilica and the papal summer residence near Rome.

The appendectomy was the sixth time the Pope had entered the Gemelli hospital since his election in 1978. The first was for emergency surgery to save his life after Turkish gunman Mehmet Ali Agca shot him in St Peter's Square in 1981.
Doctors have said the appendectomy was a success and confirmed there had been no recurrence of a colon tumour removed in 1992.
Although his recovery was proceeding well, several doctors have suggested the Pope slow down, travel less and rest more.
The surgery has also intensified attention on a violent trembling of the Pope's left hand, which some doctors say is a potential sign of Parkinson's Disease.
The Vatican has not specifically denied that the Pope is suffering from Parkinson's or a related neurological disorder.
It would not comment directly on Monday on a report by the New York Times that an announcement confirming the Pope's ailment could be imminent.
"We have not received any new information from doctors to release," chief Vatican spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said when asked to comment on the newspaper report.
The Pope's release from hospital means he will be back at the Vatican to mark the 18th anniversary on Wednesday of his election as leader of the world's Roman Catholics.

Vatican officials have said the Pope plans to celebrate his first public mass at the Vatican to mark a religious holiday on October 27. They say he is also keen to be in good shape for November 1, the 50th anniversary of his ordination as a priest.
Aides say he is likely to begin short audiences even earlier.
The Pope is due to make four foreign trips next year, to the Czech Republic, Poland, France and Brazil.
